Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to surface a couple of items before we move to legal:

- Can you confirm how upgrades/downgrades are handled mid-term? Specifically: proration, effective date, and whether feature swaps (e.g., add routing policies or extra KV cache slots) are allowed without amending the term.

From: david_kim@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Packaging options + upgrade/downgrade policy (RFP attached)

Hi Claire —

Appreciate the RFP — good detail. Quick summary and I'll assemble the single-sheet comparison for procurement: 

1) Upgrade/downgrade rules (short):
   - Upgrades: effective immediately; charge pro-rated from the date of change for the remainder of the billing period. If moving to a larger committed tier mid-term, we apply the new commitment rate forward only (no retroactive changes).
   - Downgrades: allowed at next billing cycle unless you buy-down with a one-time adjustment. We offer an early-downgrade wind-down that keeps feature parity for 30 days to ease traffic shifts (sometimes requested by customers).
   - Feature swaps: supported via add/remove SKUs. If the swap increases committed throughput, proration and commit re-calculation apply. For purely feature-only swaps (no throughput change) we usually allow a straight swap with minimal paperwork.

2) Multi-region bundling:
   - We can create a unified committed pool that spans regions (recommended for predictable burst behavior). Pricing is by committed throughput buckets + per-region egress adjustments.

3) Discount palette we typically see for your size:
   - 12-month commit: ~10% list discount (tiered by throughput)
   - 24-month commit: ~15–20% (larger throughput volumes often hit 20%)
   - We can offer an additional short-term concession for pilot conversion (one-time credit or PS hours).

I'll drop a one-page comparison and a proposal for a 12- and 24-month path (starter -> growth -> dedicated) by end of day Friday. Want me to include a sample redline for the downgrade language?

Best,
David
David Kim
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Looping in for discount/concession guidance.

David — nice summary. For NimbleCare I recommend: 
- Offer a 12-month commit at 12% off list for the growth package, with a convert-to-24 option at month 6 that applies a retroactive 3% credit to the remaining term (invoiced as a negative adjustment).
- Include a one-time 40-hour professional services credit (for integration + playbook tuning) that vest on signature.
- For downgrades: allow one free downgrade in a 12-month term (applies at next billing cycle), subsequent downgrades require a nominal buy-down equal to 25% of the remaining month difference.

This preserves commercial flexibility while protecting unit economics. I can sign off on these terms for ACV up to $350k; any larger I want a heads-up.

K
Kimberly Park
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
